Moorefield.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Moorefield calls follow the ground the town sits on: south Fork Potomac River (along the town), wide farm valley floor, forested ridges forming both valley walls. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, woodchucks, striped skunks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

The pattern repeats yearly: raccoon and squirrel denning in spring, bats and digging animals through summer, and a hard rodent and squirrel push into heated homes each fall. Moorefield is an older farm-valley town of 1800s homes and brick blocks with postwar neighborhoods around the core. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.
